about: VM’s own text. The Invention Timeline’s breakthroughs, each with its Wikidata item, its year (c. where approximate), its disciplines, and its point by the timeline’s placing rule; titles and notes are VM’s own text.

basis.curated: Set by hand where Wikidata’s facts would mislead
basis.institution-at-time: Discoverer’s institution at the time (Wikidata, dated)
basis.fallback: Place set by hand (Wikidata gives the discoverers no dated institution near it, nor a more exact place)

rows.label: Sumerian scribes count in sixties
rows.note: Accounting tablets from Uruk count in units of 60; the later Babylonian place-value form survives in our 60-minute hours and 360-degree circles.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, sumerian-sexagesimal): the fact is Wikidata Q114799’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Step Pyramid of Djoser, the first monumental stone building
rows.note: Credited to the official Imhotep, six stacked stone terraces mark the start of large-scale cut-stone architecture.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, djoser-pyramid): the fact is Wikidata Q192418’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Great Pyramid of Giza
rows.note: Squared to the cardinal points with remarkable accuracy, it stayed the tallest human-made structure for close to four thousand years.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, great-pyramid): the fact is Wikidata Q37200’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Plimpton 322 tabulates Pythagorean triples
rows.note: An Old Babylonian clay tablet lists whole-number sides of right triangles more than a thousand years before Pythagoras.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, plimpton-322): the fact is Wikidata Q1470425’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Babylonians record the cycle of Venus
rows.note: Twenty-one years of Venus appearing and vanishing, observed under King Ammisaduqa, among the oldest astronomical records kept.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, venus-tablet): the fact is Wikidata Q1309635’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Edwin Smith Papyrus, the oldest surgical treatise
rows.note: Forty-eight injury cases, each with examination, diagnosis and treatment, including the earliest known written account of the brain.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, edwin-smith-papyrus): the fact is Wikidata Q842363’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Ebers Papyrus records hundreds of remedies
rows.note: A long Egyptian medical scroll on the heart, eyes, skin and digestion, with some 700 prescriptions and spells.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, ebers-papyrus): the fact is Wikidata Q310301’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Rhind Mathematical Papyrus
rows.note: The scribe Ahmes copies 84 problems on fractions, areas, volumes and equations, with a value for π close to 3.16.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, rhind-papyrus): the fact is Wikidata Q213540’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Water clock at Karnak
rows.note: The oldest surviving water clock, an alabaster vessel from the reign of Amenhotep III, tells the night hours by its outflow.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, karnak-water-clock): the fact is Wikidata Q194173’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Shang oracle bones record eclipses
rows.note: Divination bones from the Shang capital note eclipses of the Moon, the earliest Chinese astronomical records.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, shang-eclipses): the fact is Wikidata Q283127’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Babylonian Astronomical Diaries begin
rows.note: Night-by-night records of the Moon, planets, weather and prices, kept for some six centuries: antiquity’s longest scientific record.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, astronomical-diaries): the fact is Wikidata Q751861’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Sushruta Samhita: surgery in ancient India
rows.note: A Sanskrit treatise describing hundreds of operations and instruments, including rebuilding the nose with a flap of skin.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, sushruta-samhita): the fact is Wikidata Q1995239’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Thales predicts a solar eclipse
rows.note: Herodotus reports that Thales foretold the eclipse that stopped a battle between the Lydians and the Medes.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, thales-eclipse): the fact is Wikidata Q537110’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Tunnel of Eupalinos dug from both ends
rows.note: A kilometre-long aqueduct tunnel cut from two sides that met near the middle, an early triumph of applied geometry.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, eupalinos-tunnel): the fact is Wikidata Q955894’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Pythagoreans: number underlies nature
rows.note: The community Pythagoras led at Croton treats number as the key to the world; the right-triangle theorem carries his name.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, pythagoreans): the fact is Wikidata Q11518’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Alcmaeon places the mind in the brain
rows.note: From dissection he traces the optic nerves and argues that the brain, not the heart, is the seat of perception and thought.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, alcmaeon): its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Leucippus and Democritus propose atoms
rows.note: Everything is made of tiny indivisible particles moving in empty space, a guess chemistry would vindicate two millennia later.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, atomism): the fact is Wikidata Q178668’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Hippocratic medicine: disease has natural causes
rows.note: The Hippocratic writings explain illness without the gods and stress observation, prognosis and a physician’s duties.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, hippocratic-medicine): the fact is Wikidata Q1135155’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Eudoxus: proportion, exhaustion and nested spheres
rows.note: A theory of ratios that copes with irrational lengths, the method of exhaustion, and the first geometric model of the planets.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, eudoxus): its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Aristotle’s History of Animals founds zoology
rows.note: Hundreds of species, many studied on Lesbos, described and grouped by anatomy, reproduction and way of life.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, aristotle-zoology): the fact is Wikidata Q1620799’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Euclid’s Elements
rows.note: Thirteen books that derive geometry and number theory from definitions and axioms, the model of proof for two thousand years.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, euclid-elements): the fact is Wikidata Q172891’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Theophrastus classifies plants
rows.note: Some 500 plants described by form, habitat and use, earning Aristotle’s successor the title of father of botany.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, theophrastus-plants): the fact is Wikidata Q17156420’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Herophilus dissects the human body
rows.note: Systematic human dissection separates nerves from tendons, describes the brain’s ventricles and ties the pulse to the heart.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, herophilus): its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Aristarchus puts the Sun at the centre
rows.note: Reckoning that the Sun is far larger than the Earth, he proposes that the Earth goes round it, 1,800 years before Copernicus.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, aristarchus): the fact is Wikidata Q7091541’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Archimedes: buoyancy and the lever
rows.note: A floating body displaces its own weight of fluid; with the law of the lever, the first results of statics and hydrostatics.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, archimedes-buoyancy): the fact is Wikidata Q181404’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Archimedes pins π between 3 10⁄71 and 3 1⁄7
rows.note: Polygons of 96 sides drawn inside and outside a circle squeeze π between two fractions, an early limit argument.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, archimedes-pi): the fact is Wikidata Q511915’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Ctesibius: the force pump and a self-regulating clock
rows.note: Machines driven by air and water pressure, including a float-regulated water clock that set the pattern for centuries.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, ctesibius): its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Eratosthenes measures the Earth
rows.note: Noon shadows at Syene and Alexandria give a circumference close to the true 40,000 km.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, eratosthenes): its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Apollonius names the conic sections
rows.note: Ellipse, parabola and hyperbola studied as slices of a cone: the curves Kepler and Newton would need.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, apollonius-conics): the fact is Wikidata Q3828633’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Hipparchus finds precession and begins trigonometry
rows.note: Comparing his star positions with older ones reveals the slow drift of the equinoxes; his table of chords starts trigonometry.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, hipparchus): the fact is Wikidata Q83094’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Antikythera mechanism
rows.note: Recovered from a shipwreck, this geared bronze calculator modelled the Sun and Moon, predicted eclipses and tracked the games.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, antikythera): the fact is Wikidata Q182324’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: The Yellow Emperor’s Inner Classic
rows.note: The founding text of Chinese medicine: organs, channels, pulse diagnosis and the balance of yin and yang.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, huangdi-neijing): the fact is Wikidata Q428448’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Maya Long Count calendar
rows.note: Stela 2 at Chiapa de Corzo carries the oldest known Long Count date; Maya place-value numbers came to include a zero.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, maya-long-count): the fact is Wikidata Q767358’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Vitruvius writes On Architecture
rows.note: Ten books on building, water supply, machines and sundials, the only major work on architecture surviving from antiquity.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, vitruvius): the fact is Wikidata Q1232238’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Hero of Alexandria spins a sphere with steam
rows.note: The aeolipile, turned by jets of steam, appears among Hero’s pneumatic devices, automata and surveying instruments.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, hero-aeolipile): the fact is Wikidata Q338613’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Pliny’s Natural History
rows.note: A 37-book encyclopedia of astronomy, geography, animals, plants, medicine and minerals, read throughout the Middle Ages.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, pliny-natural-history): the fact is Wikidata Q442’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Cai Lun improves papermaking
rows.note: A court official presents paper made from bark, hemp, rags and old fishing nets: cheap writing material that spread across Asia.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, papermaking): the fact is Wikidata Q11472’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: The Pantheon’s concrete dome
rows.note: Roman concrete with volcanic ash spans 43 metres, still the largest unreinforced concrete dome in the world.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, pantheon-dome): the fact is Wikidata Q99309’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Zhang Heng’s seismoscope
rows.note: A bronze vessel that dropped a ball from a dragon’s mouth to signal a distant earthquake and the direction it came from.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, zhang-heng-seismoscope): its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Ptolemy’s Almagest
rows.note: An Earth-centred model of epicycles and equants that predicted planetary positions well enough to be used for 1,400 years.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, almagest): the fact is Wikidata Q155952’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Ptolemy maps the world by coordinates
rows.note: Thousands of places listed by latitude and longitude, with instructions for projecting the globe onto a flat map.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, ptolemy-geography): the fact is Wikidata Q1194350’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Galen’s experimental physiology
rows.note: Experiments on animals show that arteries carry blood and that cutting nerves from the spine paralyses muscles.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, galen): its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Diophantus writes the Arithmetica
rows.note: Problems solved with abbreviations for unknowns and powers, an early step towards algebraic notation.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, diophantus): the fact is Wikidata Q668560’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Liu Hui’s commentary on the Nine Chapters
rows.note: Proofs for the classic Chinese problem book, with negative numbers, elimination for linear systems and π ≈ 3.1416.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, liu-hui): the fact is Wikidata Q657057’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Hypatia teaches mathematics and astronomy
rows.note: Head of a philosophical school, she wrote commentaries on Diophantus and Apollonius and helped edit Ptolemy’s Almagest.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, hypatia): its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Zu Chongzhi computes π to seven digits
rows.note: π lies between 3.1415926 and 3.1415927, with the fraction 355/113: a record that stood for almost a thousand years.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, zu-chongzhi): the fact is Wikidata Q3858176’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Aryabhata’s Aryabhatiya
rows.note: Place-value arithmetic, a sine table, π ≈ 3.1416 and the proposal that the Earth turns on its axis.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, aryabhatiya): the fact is Wikidata Q3518429’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Philoponus challenges Aristotle’s physics
rows.note: Heavy and light bodies fall at nearly the same speed, and a thrown object keeps an impressed force, an early idea of impetus.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, philoponus): its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Hagia Sophia’s dome on pendentives
rows.note: Two mathematicians design a vast dome carried on curved triangles over a square plan, a new solution in engineering.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, hagia-sophia): the fact is Wikidata Q12506’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Brahmagupta gives rules for zero and negatives
rows.note: The first text to treat zero as a number, with rules for adding, subtracting and multiplying debts, fortunes and zero.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, brahmagupta-zero): the fact is Wikidata Q1290001’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Sun Simiao’s prescriptions worth a thousand gold
rows.note: A thirty-volume medical encyclopedia covering women’s and children’s health and diet, opening with a code of medical ethics.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, sun-simiao): its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Dunhuang Star Chart
rows.note: The oldest complete star atlas known, drawing well over a thousand stars of the Chinese sky.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, dunhuang-star-chart): the fact is Wikidata Q5315281’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Yi Xing’s water-driven celestial globe
rows.note: A water-powered globe with an escapement-like mechanism to mark the hours; Yi Xing also led a nationwide survey of the meridian.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, yi-xing): its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Laboratory alchemy of the Jabirian corpus
rows.note: Writings attributed to Jabir describe distillation, crystallisation and the preparation of acids, and sort substances by their properties.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, jabirian-alchemy): its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Al-Khwarizmi’s algebra
rows.note: Systematic solution of linear and quadratic equations; “algebra” comes from the book’s title and “algorithm” from his name.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, al-khwarizmi-algebra): the fact is Wikidata Q8369’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Al-Kindi invents frequency analysis
rows.note: Substitution ciphers are broken by counting how often each letter occurs: the start of cryptanalysis.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, al-kindi-cryptanalysis): the fact is Wikidata Q565636’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: The Banu Musa’s Book of Ingenious Devices
rows.note: About a hundred mechanisms, from automatic valves and self-trimming lamps to a programmable mechanical flute player.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, banu-musa): the fact is Wikidata Q4116191’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Chinese alchemists discover gunpowder
rows.note: A Taoist text warns that heating saltpetre, sulphur and charcoal together makes flames burst out: the first record of gunpowder.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, gunpowder): the fact is Wikidata Q12861’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Al-Battani measures the solar year
rows.note: Decades of observations at Raqqa give the length of the year to within about two minutes and improve on Ptolemy’s values.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, al-battani): its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Al-Razi tells smallpox from measles
rows.note: His treatise on smallpox and measles gives the first clear clinical description separating the two diseases.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, al-razi): its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Al-Sufi’s Book of Fixed Stars
rows.note: An illustrated star catalogue with the first written description of the Andromeda Galaxy, a “small cloud”.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, al-sufi): the fact is Wikidata Q2087785’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Ibn Sahl states the law of refraction
rows.note: A treatise on burning mirrors and lenses gives the sine law of refraction six centuries before Snell.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, ibn-sahl): the fact is Wikidata Q208391’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Al-Zahrawi’s illustrated surgery
rows.note: The last volume of his medical encyclopedia draws some 200 surgical instruments and was used in European schools for centuries.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, al-zahrawi): the fact is Wikidata Q2724312’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Ibn al-Haytham’s Book of Optics
rows.note: Experiments with light, mirrors and the camera obscura show that we see by light entering the eye: a model of experimental method.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, book-of-optics): the fact is Wikidata Q264562’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Al-Biruni measures the Earth from a hilltop
rows.note: The dip of the horizon seen from a hill near Nandana gives the Earth’s radius to within a few per cent.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, al-biruni-radius): its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Avicenna’s Canon of Medicine
rows.note: A five-book synthesis of Greek and Islamic medicine with rules for testing drugs, taught in Europe until the 1600s.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, canon-of-medicine): the fact is Wikidata Q466060’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Bi Sheng invents movable type
rows.note: Characters of baked clay set in an iron frame, described by Shen Kuo, four centuries before Gutenberg.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, movable-type): the fact is Wikidata Q426853’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Song astronomers record the Crab supernova
rows.note: A “guest star” bright enough to see by day for 23 days; its remnant is the Crab Nebula.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, sn-1054): the fact is Wikidata Q32037’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Omar Khayyam: cubic equations and a new calendar
rows.note: He classifies and solves cubic equations with conic sections, and leads the reform of the Jalali solar calendar at Isfahan.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, khayyam): its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Shen Kuo describes the magnetic compass
rows.note: The Dream Pool Essays describe a magnetised-needle compass and magnetic declination, and argue that landscapes change over time.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, dream-pool-essays): the fact is Wikidata Q1069875’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Su Song’s astronomical clock tower
rows.note: A twelve-metre water-driven tower with an escapement that turned an armillary sphere and a celestial globe and struck the hours.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, su-song-clock): its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Bhaskara II’s Crown of Treatises
rows.note: The head of the Ujjain observatory solves Pell’s equation by the cyclic method and touches on ideas of the derivative.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, bhaskara): the fact is Wikidata Q3448458’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Hildegard of Bingen’s natural history
rows.note: Books on plants, animals, stones and remedies, the first natural history and medicine written by a woman in Germany.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, hildegard): its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Al-Idrisi’s world map for Roger II
rows.note: Fifteen years of travellers’ reports compiled at Palermo make the most accurate world map of the Middle Ages.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, tabula-rogeriana): the fact is Wikidata Q1089336’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Fibonacci’s Liber Abaci
rows.note: Hindu–Arabic numerals and place-value arithmetic for European merchants, with the rabbit problem behind the Fibonacci numbers.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, liber-abaci): the fact is Wikidata Q2044496’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Al-Jazari’s Book of Ingenious Mechanical Devices
rows.note: Fifty machines, from crank-driven pumps to programmable automata, each drawn with instructions for building it.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, al-jazari): the fact is Wikidata Q102112338’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Ibn al-Nafis describes the pulmonary circulation
rows.note: Blood passes from the right side of the heart to the left through the lungs, not through pores in the wall as Galen taught.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, ibn-al-nafis): the fact is Wikidata Q494603’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: The Maragheh observatory and the Tusi couple
rows.note: Al-Tusi’s observatory produces new tables, and his two rolling circles turn circular motion into straight-line motion.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, maragheh-tusi): the fact is Wikidata Q1035674’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Roger Bacon’s Opus Majus urges experiment
rows.note: A treatise for the Pope on optics, mathematics and “experimental science”, describing lenses that magnify.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, opus-majus): the fact is Wikidata Q4373704’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Peter Peregrinus defines magnetic poles
rows.note: Written during the siege of Lucera, the letter describes north and south poles, attraction and repulsion, and a pivoted compass.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, peregrinus-magnet): its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Guo Shoujing’s Season-Granting calendar
rows.note: New instruments and a network of observatories fix the year at 365.2425 days, the value of the later Gregorian calendar.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, shoushi-calendar): the fact is Wikidata Q11077930’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Eyeglasses invented in Italy
rows.note: A Pisan sermon of 1306 says spectacles had been invented about twenty years before: convex lenses for reading.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, eyeglasses): the fact is Wikidata Q37501’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Mondino de Luzzi’s manual of dissection
rows.note: Written from public dissections at Bologna, his Anathomia was the standard anatomy text for two centuries.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, mondino-anatomy): its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Richard of Wallingford’s astronomical clock
rows.note: Designed for St Albans Abbey, a mechanical clock showing the Sun, Moon, tides and eclipses, among the most complex of its age.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, wallingford-clock): its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Oxford Calculators prove the mean speed theorem
rows.note: A uniformly accelerating body covers the same distance as one moving at its mean speed, a result Galileo later used.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, mean-speed-theorem): the fact is Wikidata Q6803664’s; its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Ibn al-Shatir’s planetary models
rows.note: Models of the Moon and planets without Ptolemy’s equant, matching ones Copernicus used two centuries later.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, ibn-al-shatir): its title and note are VM’s own text

rows.label: Oresme draws graphs of changing quantities
rows.note: Plotting intensity against time anticipates coordinate graphs and gives a geometric proof of the mean speed theorem.

date.line: Invention Timeline (science/progress/data/events.json, oresme): its title and note are VM’s own text
